db_evidence.notes: The memory DB (episodes/event_steps/visual_clips/semantic_triples) contains no text mentioning small monsters near the tree at either collection; text search for '落伽香藤'/'香藤' returns only unrelated rows or the pickup-adjacent episode text without monster detail, so this question is unanswerable from text alone and requires clip_qa. All 5 rollouts DID converge on run_sql/semantic_search producing the roughly correct 30-90s windows around at least one of the two true clue intervals (64800-64920s and/or 74400-75600s), so the DB is not the bottleneck for locating the general time region. The bottleneck is entirely in how clip_qa was instructed to define 'the moment of collection' and how far back it looked.

root_causes: Systematic mis-scoping of 'when collecting X' as the single frame where the on-screen item-pickup notification appears, rather than the whole collection encounter; the true clue interval (64802-64806) is ~12-16s before the notification frame (64818s) because the player first fights through 4 small monsters guarding the tree, then the pickup completes once the area is cleared. 4 of 5 rollouts (0,1,3-partial,4) hit this exact failure for the first occurrence.

When re-querying a broader window did surface the correct count (rollout 3, clip_qa on 64770-64830 -> 4), the agent then mislabeled a nearby but unrelated interval (64920-65010, ~100s after the first collection) as the 'second' occurrence instead of navigating to the true second clue interval at 75150-75156s, so it never checked the right place for the second count.

One rollout (2) never anchored on the correct first-occurrence time window at all, instead reporting collection events at 67301.5s and 70780.0s that don't match either clue interval, indicating its semantic_search/run_sql exploration drifted to unrelated tree/collect-flavored episodes without cross-checking the entity's actual (single, correct) first appearance near 64800s.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly identified 火焰山/Flaming Mountains context and used semantic_search + run_sql to narrow toward plausible time windows containing '落伽香藤' or tree-collection events, despite the DB having no monster-count text for these events.
3 of 5 rollouts (0, 1, 4) correctly bracketed both true clue intervals (~64800-64920s and ~74400-75600s) with clip_qa calls, and correctly got the second count (0) right.

Rollout 3, by re-issuing clip_qa with an explicitly widened temporal framing ('inspect the moments just before and during collection' rather than 'at the collection moment'), successfully recovered the correct first count of 4, showing the sub-agent COULD see the monsters when the video window and prompt covered the pre-pickup fight.
transferable_lessons: For 'how many X near Y when collecting Z' questions in this game-footage domain, treat the pickup-notification text overlay as the END of the encounter, not the query target: widen the clip_qa video window and prompt to explicitly search the ~10-20s leading up to the notification for combat/monster presence, not just the notification frame itself.

When a question says 'first and second time', after finding the first occurrence's true timestamp, don't accept the next nearby candidate as the second; explicitly search for the *next* text/entity mention of the exact item across the whole rest of the timeline (e.g. entities/semantic_triples/event_steps LIKE the item name ordered by start_s) before invoking clip_qa on a guessed second window, so as not to confuse a proximate unrelated encounter (e.g. 64920-65010s) with the true, temporally distant second occurrence (75150s).

If clip_qa returns 0 for a scene that intuitively should contain combat (e.g. a boss/monster HP bar or spark/attack VFX visible in nearby frames pulled during sampling), re-issue with a wider start_s margin and an instruction to scan the full lead-in period, not just the exact frame matching the query text overlay.
open_questions: Whether the reference '4' for the first occurrence should be interpreted strictly as 'monsters visible in the single frame right when the item is picked up' (in which case the reference itself would be inconsistent with what all 5 clip_qa calls observed at 64818s) or as 'monsters encountered during that collection episode' (which the ground-truth frames at 64802-64809s support); resolving this matters for whether the reference answer's intended framing matches what the judge is scoring against.
